project.name: Bifrost Integrations
project.summary: An open-source automation platform for MSP integration work. A React web app talks to a FastAPI control plane, which stores everything in PostgreSQL and Redis, keeps files in S3-compatible storage, and hands workflow and AI-agent runs to execution workers. A scheduler drives recurring work, a CLI and an MCP gateway let other tools drive the platform, and a small app runtime lets people build and host their own React apps inside it.

tour.title: Start with the app people use
tour.note: A single React app. Left to right, it holds the list screens (workflows, forms, agents, tables, integrations), the editors, the chat, and a settings area.

tour.title: Every button becomes a request
tour.note: Each of these files is one group of web addresses. A screen calls one, and the handler checks who is asking before anything happens.

tour.title: Where the real rules live
tour.note: Handlers stay thin. The thinking - permissions, OAuth, builds, deployments, agent runs - happens in these services, which is why it is the biggest part of the platform.

tour.title: Where slow work actually runs
tour.note: Workflows and agents need minutes, not milliseconds, so the API hands them to separated worker processes. These run the code, stream the logs back, and record the result.

tour.title: What the platform remembers
tour.note: Almost everything durable is a PostgreSQL row: organizations, users, roles, workflows, runs, jobs. Redis holds caches and live channels; S3 holds files and built apps.

tour.title: How it talks to other systems
tour.note: Connections, OAuth tokens, Git sync and manifests all live here. This is what lets one workflow talk to NinjaOne on Monday and HaloPSA on Tuesday.

tour.title: Apps built inside Bifrost
tour.note: People can build their own React apps against the platform. This part compiles them, serves the SDK and renders them, which is why Bifrost can host dashboards as well as automations.

nodes.label: Chat & agents

nodes.label: Admin screens' parts

nodes.label: Design kit

nodes.label: Data & state

nodes.label: Platform API
nodes.summary: The FastAPI control plane: sign-in, tenants, permissions, workflows, agents, apps, Solutions, files and every endpoint the app and CLI call.

nodes.label: Endpoints
nodes.summary: One file per group of web addresses; each handler checks access, then hands the work to a service.

nodes.label: Business logic
nodes.summary: The rules and the heavy lifting: OAuth flows, builds, deployments, agent runs, Git sync and access checks.

nodes.label: Agents & AI

nodes.label: Apps & SDK

nodes.label: Integrations & sync

nodes.label: Solutions

nodes.label: Access & identity
nodes.summary: Who may see or change what: roles, permissions, organization scoping, MFA, passkeys and sign-in identities.

nodes.label: Knowledge & search
nodes.summary: Indexes documents and source code so agents and people can search them, including embeddings and retrieval.

nodes.label: Files & artifacts
nodes.summary: Stores and serves files, keeps the searchable file index, and generates artifacts such as documents and images.

nodes.label: Jobs, events & ops
nodes.summary: The platform's own housekeeping and durable work: platform jobs, notifications, audit, metrics, retention and Kubernetes isolation.

nodes.label: Core plumbing
nodes.summary: The shared foundation of the API: database sessions, Redis, caching, CSRF, rate limits, auth context and settings.

nodes.label: Repositories
nodes.summary: The only code that reads and writes stored records, keeping organization scoping consistent.

nodes.label: Execution Workers
nodes.summary: Separate processes that actually run workflows and agents, stream their logs and report results back to the API.

nodes.label: Worker launcher
nodes.summary: Starts a worker, keeps it healthy, and lets it claim and run work handed out by the API.

nodes.label: Execution engine
nodes.summary: Loads a workflow's code, runs it in a sandboxed process, and captures logs, memory, CPU and the result.

nodes.label: Worker pool
nodes.summary: Decides how much memory and capacity each worker has and how runs are spread across them.

nodes.label: Scheduler process
nodes.summary: The scheduler container: heartbeats, runs the launcher, and manages Kubernetes control when deployed there.

nodes.label: Jobs & Scheduled Tasks
nodes.summary: The durable job system and every recurring loop: builds, deploys, exports, token refresh, retention and cleanup.

nodes.label: Durable jobs
nodes.summary: Long operations that survive a restart: each one has status, progress, retries, cancellation and a place in PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: Recurring loops
nodes.summary: Time-based work: cron triggers, OAuth token refresh, webhook renewal, retention, cleanups and metrics sampling.

nodes.label: Consumers
nodes.summary: Background consumers that pick up queued work and run it outside a request.

nodes.label: Bifrost CLI
nodes.summary: The `bifrost` command people use from a terminal: create and edit entities, sync a workspace, deploy Solutions and drive the API.

nodes.label: Commands
nodes.summary: One module per entity type, so `bifrost workflows ...`, `bifrost apps ...` and friends behave the same way.

nodes.label: CLI contracts

nodes.label: Terminal UI
nodes.summary: Interactive terminal screens for file selection, progress and sync.

nodes.label: Server & auth

nodes.label: Client

nodes.label: App platform

nodes.label: Build service

nodes.label: Tables
nodes.summary: The database tables as Python classes, one file per area of the product.

nodes.label: API shapes
nodes.summary: The request and response shapes every endpoint, the CLI and the generated TypeScript types agree on.

nodes.label: Migrations
nodes.summary: The ordered changes that turn an older database into the current schema.

nodes.label: Shared Business Logic
nodes.summary: Rules used by both the API and the workers, so a permission or file decision means the same thing everywhere.

nodes.label: Access rules

nodes.label: Workflow SDK

nodes.label: Execution & events

nodes.label: Deploy & CI

nodes.label: Kubernetes
nodes.summary: Used to run heavy build and deploy jobs in temporary pods, sized from what each job actually needed last time.

edges.label: hands out runs
edges.description: The API records an execution and makes it claimable; a worker leases it and runs it. Nothing long runs inside a request.

edges.label: claims, logs, results
edges.description: Workers report progress and results through the API's worker control channel.

edges.label: cache & channels
edges.description: Cached modules, sessions and WebSocket fan-out.

edges.label: files, apps, artifacts
edges.description: Workspace files, built app bundles and generated artifacts.

edges.label: isolated build pods
edges.description: Build-class jobs such as app deploys and Solution exports run in temporary pods.

edges.label: runs the build
edges.description: A deploy job calls the app compiler and bundler, then records the new deployment.

edges.label: stores built apps
edges.description: Each successful build writes its bundle to file storage for the live app to load.

edges.label: serves the live bundle
edges.description: The app host loads the active bundle through the API rather than from a build on the client.

edges.label: webhooks & pushes
edges.description: GitHub calls the API when a connected repository changes.

edges.label: OAuth & Graph
edges.description: Token exchange and Graph calls for connected Microsoft tenants.

edges.label: model calls
edges.description: Every agent and chat turn is a model request through the configured provider.

edges.label: SDK calls
edges.description: A hosted app reaches platform data only through the public API.

annotations.note: The shared CLI/SDK contract. A change here can break installed CLIs, so version gates live next to it.
The canonical durable-job system. New long-running work should extend this rather than add its own job table.
Every screen's requests pass through here, including sign-in expiry and error shaping.

flows.title: Run a workflow
flows.description: What happens between someone pressing Run and seeing the result.

steps.note: Someone fills in a form or presses Run on a workflow
POST to the executions endpoint, after a permission check
The API records the run, picks the workflow version and makes it claimable
A worker claims the run, loads the Python and executes it in a sandboxed process
The workflow calls tables, files, integrations and AI through the workflow SDK
Results and logs are written back as rows, and the screen updates live

flows.title: Build and publish an app
flows.description: How a custom React app goes from the editor to a URL people can open.

steps.note: The author edits the app's files in the browser editor
Saving and deploying go through the app endpoints
The deploy becomes a durable platform job instead of a long request
The compiler and bundler build the app against the current SDK
The built bundle is stored and activated as the live deployment
The host fetches the live bundle and mounts the app with the SDK

flows.title: Ask an agent
flows.description: A chat message becoming an answer with real tool calls.

steps.note: Someone types a question into the chat
The chat endpoint starts a run for the chosen agent
Prompts, model choice, tools, budgets and retries are assembled here
The model is called with the tools it is allowed to use
The run executes outside the request, calling platform tools and recording every step
Steps, tool results and the answer stream back to the conversation
